newsitem.title: USA: NYC bar welcomes draft ABA pay-to-play resolution.
newsitem.headline: NYC bar welcomes draft ABA pay-to-play resolution.

text.p: New York City's prestigious bar association said Wednesday that the "pay-to-play" resolution that American Bar Association delegates will vote on next month is a step in the right direction.
"This proposed resolution, if enacted, would be a welcome step forward," Michael Cardozo, president of the Association of the Bar of the City of New York, said in a written statement.
ABA's policy making body will vote on the proposal condemning pay-to-play at the group's annual meeting in San Francisco, which runs from July 31 to August 6.
The policy also asks ABA's president to appoint a task force to study the issue and suggest possible solutions.
Pay-to-play refers to bond professionals who give contributions to elected officials in return for bond business or consideration for bond business.
The New York City bar earlier this year called for a much stronger policy.
It said that if a lawyer contributes to an elected municipal official, the attorney and his or her firm may not do public finance business with that locality for two years.
But the group recently agreed to sign on to the draft ABA plan after ABA panels strongly opposed City bar's version.

"We hope that ultimately the ABA task force will develop recommendations for specific rules and regulations to guide these efforts nationally as we continue to urge New York to enact appropriate rules banning pay-to-play," Cardozo said.
Following is the draft resolution.
"Resolved, that the American Bar Association:

1) condemns the practice of lawyers making political campaign contributions to, and soliciting ... contributions for, public officials in return for being considered eligible by public agencies to perform professional services, including municipal finance engagements;

2) calls upon bar associations, lawyer disciplinary agencies and the judiciary to enforce, when applicable to prohibit this practice, existing Rules of Professional Conduct, such as (ABA) Model Rule 7.2(c) prohibiting a lawyer from giving 'anything of value to a person for recommending the lawyer's services';

3) condemns the practice of public officials considering as eligible for engagement by public agencies to perform professional services, including municipal finance engagements, only those lawyers who make political campaign contributions to, or solicit ... contributions for, public officials; and

4) calls upon legislative bodies, judicial rule-making agencies, bar associations, lawyer disciplinary agencies and public agencies to enact or adopt and enforce laws, rules and regulations that will discourage the practices condemned in these resolutions.
Further resolved, that (ABA's) House of Delegates requests the President of the American Bar Association to appoint a task force:

a) to review issues related to political campaign contributions made or solicited by lawyers and effective solutions thereto, including the 'pay-to-play' rule proposed by the Association of the Bar of the City of New York;

b) to determine whether additional professional standards, laws or procedures relating to the practices condemned in these resolutions are necessary and desirable, including the practice of lawyers making significant political campaign contributions to judicial candidates before whom the lawyers appear; and

c) to submit for consideration by (ABA's) House of Delegates at its meeting in August 1998 recommendations as to any additional professional standards, laws or procedures found to be necessary and desirable in the form of amendments to the Model Rules of Professional Condut, aspirational ethical standards or other appropriate measures."
--Vicky Stamas, U.S. Municipals Desk, 202-898-8314
